summary: Ten experiments completed in 8.8 minutes, including five compute-bound experiments. Verifier-committed uncertainty routing, gated on Exp7129 bank was longest at 5.55 minutes, but the supplied evidence gives no causal phase breakdown and the locked field records no GPU-idle event on compute-bound work.
bottlenecks_identified: Verifier-committed uncertainty routing, gated on Exp7129 bank occupied 5.55 of the 8.8 minutes; no data available this milestone explains why.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides elapsed durations but no phase spans, so setup, queueing, model loading, inference, and verification costs cannot be separated.
The GPU monitor snapshot is not correlated with an active experiment, so it cannot establish accelerator efficiency during compute-bound execution.
No data available this milestone establishes a concurrent two-or-more-model task or a missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic start, stop, and phase timestamps for every experiment instead of relying only on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Attach experiment identity and active phase to GPU utilization samples so compute-task idle periods can be distinguished from correct synthesis-only idle periods.
Emit model-count and runner-choice launch receipts, and select DualGPURunner when two or more independent models are loaded in parallel while retaining single-GPU dispatch for single-model work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add per-experiment monotonic phase spans to localize the 5.55-minute critical path.
Add task-correlated GPU sampling with compute-bound and active-phase labels.
Record launch-time model count and runner choice, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch only for parallel two-or-more-model workloads.
meta_reflection: This retrospective separates observed duration from unmeasured cause: the critical path is visible, but its expensive phase is not. The savings estimate remains 0 because no timed alternative or intervention effect is available this milestone.
